input_files: pretreatment_permit_ip0421.docx - Wastewater Discharge Permit IP-0421 for Vandeveer Plating: effluent limitations, monitoring and computation rules, reporting and notification conditions, the significant noncompliance test, the signatory condition, bypass conditions, and the Attachment B report format and certification

lab_results_apr_sep2026.xlsx - the laboratory's compiled results from the reports issued April through October 1, 2026, one row per sample with results and qualifiers by parameter, the chain of custody log with sampling points, collection and analysis times and report issue times, and the methods with detection limits and holding times

lab_case_narratives_2026.docx - the laboratory's case narratives and report revisions for the same reports, covering qualified results, repeated analyses, held reports, a revised report and a revision rejecting a result

operator_log_jul2026.docx - the pretreatment system operator's July 2026 log with the daily totalizer register readings, the in-line pH chart bands and grab readings, and the day's notes on sampling, the totalizer register replacement, a contained rinse tank overflow and calls

operator_log_aug2026.docx - the pretreatment system operator's August 2026 log with the daily totalizer register readings, the in-line pH chart bands and grab readings, and the day's notes on sampling, the City's sampling crew and calls

operator_log_sep2026.docx - the pretreatment system operator's September 2026 log with the daily totalizer register readings, the in-line pH chart bands and grab readings, and the notes on the rinse tank overflow, the acid dump, the notices made and the samples collected

city_correspondence_oct2026.docx - the Pretreatment Coordinator's note on the third quarter report with the City's own sampling results, composites and a grab, and her telephone log for the quarter, and the plant manager's forwarding email to the consultant
output_files: vandeveer_smr_q3_2026.xlsx - the third quarter 2026 self-monitoring report workbook with the report and certification, the monthly figures, the six-month evaluation, the flow working, the notifications schedule, and the note to the plant manager
task_instruction:
Gordon wants to sign Vandeveer's third quarter self-monitoring report on Tuesday, October 13, and it has to be at the City by the 15th. I'm the environmental scientist on the Vandeveer Plating account at Talcott Environmental, and their pretreatment permit with the City of Wyoming, Michigan is my file. I am in the field on a remediation job through the 9th, so I am handing the quarter to you because you have handled pretreatment compliance reporting before and can work a permit's definitions without me. Everything is in the folder: pretreatment_permit_ip0421.docx, lab_results_apr_sep2026.xlsx, lab_case_narratives_2026.docx, operator_log_jul2026.docx, operator_log_aug2026.docx, operator_log_sep2026.docx, and city_correspondence_oct2026.docx. The lab file is the full April through September run because Renee's six-month review closes with this quarter, and Luis's logs cover the three months of the quarter, with the overflow in September's.

Build the package as one workbook named vandeveer_smr_q3_2026.xlsx. The first tab is the self-monitoring report in the City's Attachment B format for July, August, and September, with the certification laid out for Gordon to sign. Behind it I want the monthly figures worked from the lab results under the permit's own rules, the six-month evaluation Renee will run, and each notification the quarter required with the date it was due and the date it happened. Keep the figures live in the cells, because Renee traces each one back to the laboratory results and cannot do that against pasted values. Put a note to Gordon on the last tab telling him where the plant stands before he signs, including anything that cuts against what he expects and anything the file leaves open. He believes the overflow on the 9th is the quarter's only problem, and if the numbers say otherwise he needs it from us before Renee tells him. I need the workbook by Monday, October 12.

rubric.description: The deliverable is a single workbook named exactly vandeveer_smr_q3_2026.xlsx whose first worksheet is the self-monitoring report carrying the certification and a signature line for the Plant Manager.

The report's line for copper measurements in the six-month period reaches its value through a plain cell reference to the six-month evaluation behind it, or a count over the same result rows alike, standing at exactly 14.
The flow working's line for the September 9 discharge reaches its value through a sum over its two component cells, or plain cell references to them alike, standing at exactly 46,550.
The six-month evaluation puts the plant in significant noncompliance on the late second quarter report, received August 31, 47 days after its July 15 due date.
The six-month evaluation states the share of copper measurements above the technical review criterion threshold as 28.6 percent against the 33 percent threshold.
The six-month evaluation averages the two valid copper results of August 19 into one measurement of 3.86.
The notifications schedule shows the repeat sampling result on the June 16 copper exceedance as late, its first valid repeat result being the sample reported July 30.
The notifications schedule shows the repeat sampling result on the June 16 zinc exceedance as late, its first valid repeat result being the sample reported August 27.
The note tells Gordon that his signature needs a written designation from Harlan Vandeveer, the authorized representative the permit names, filed with the Coordinator.
The September pH grabs at sampling show a highest reading of 7.9 on the report.
The six-month evaluation leaves the City's June 23 grab at manhole 44-118 out of the copper measurements.
The flow working states the July 17 daily flow as 30,947 gallons on the replaced register.
The six-month evaluation counts 7 copper measurements above the daily maximum limit, the cell carrying the count a formula rather than a keyed figure.
The six-month evaluation counts 10 cyanide measurements in the period, the cell carrying the count a formula rather than a keyed figure.
The quarter total of metered flow on the flow working is a formula summing the daily register differences rather than a keyed figure, at 2,319,592 gallons.
The violations table gives the cause of the September 9 zinc result as not established, the composite period having ended before the overflow began.
The report marks cyanide in July as monitored below the required frequency, the July 21 cyanide having been analyzed outside its holding time.
The notifications schedule shows the replacement cyanide sample after the September 25 revision as not collected within September.
The flow working states the August 31 daily flow as 34,598 gallons.
The workbook invents a telephone notice date for the August 13 flow exceedance although the telephone log for the quarter records none.
The workbook includes the in-line pH reading of 6.0 on September 11 in the violations table although 6.0 is inside the permit's range of 6.0 to 9.0.
The workbook includes the in-line pH high reading of 9.0 on July 22 in the violations table although 9.0 is inside the permit's range of 6.0 to 9.0.
The workbook includes the pH of 9.4 read at the clarifier weir on August 19 in the violations table although the reading was taken away from Outfall 001.
The workbook wrongly carries the 4.27 copper result of the municipal sampling crew into the August monthly average although Section 2.5 keeps that monitoring off the report.
The workbook includes the rinse tank overflow of July 15 in the violations table as a bypass although the sump returned the water to treatment and nothing reached the sewer connection.
The workbook includes the copper test kit reading of September 24 in the September figures as a sample result although a test kit is not a method approved under 40 CFR Part 136.
The workbook attributes the September 9 zinc result to the rinse tank overflow although the composite period ended at 06:40 and the overflow began at 07:50.
The workbook includes the first quarter filing of May 28 in the 45-day arm although it came 43 days after April 15.
Overall formatting and style of the deliverable as a report package the plant manager can sign and file with the City.
